title: Dedicated throughput playbook: crediting model, escalation ladder, and contract-ready language
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Purpose:
This ticket captures a production-ready playbook for defining Dedicated throughput guarantees in customer contracts. It covers (1) precise SLO definitions for throughput commitments, (2) an error-budget accounting model for sustained or transient degradations, (3) a crediting and remediation matrix customers can include in MSA/SOW language, and (4) the operational escalation ladder that ties to autoscaling policies and fleet controls. The goal is to provide legal-safe, measurable clauses plus an internal runbook for validation and credit issuance.

Guiding principles:
- Measurability: every guarantee must map to a single metric we can compute from observed telemetry (per-customer observed throughput vs committed throughput) with clearly defined windows and aggregation rules.
- Predictability: crediting should be deterministic and capped; remediation paths should favor capacity fixes (scale/burst) before financial credits where possible.
- Composability: the model must work with dedicated capacity variants (reserved pools, burst buckets, regional pools) and integrate with autoscaling behavior.
- Customer clarity: contract language needs examples and a simple chart for how credits accrue and how partial degradations are handled.

SLO / metric definition (recommended canonical form):
- Metric name: ObservedCommittedThroughputRatio (OCTR)
- Calculation: For each billing window W (see windowing rules below), OCTR = (Total successful completed tokens served to the customer in W) / (Committed tokens promised in W).
- SLO threshold: OCTR >= 0.99 for a 30-day contractual window (example).
- Success definition: "successful completed tokens" excludes requests that fail due to client error (4xx) and excludes retried duplicate requests; includes streamed partial responses only when final status is 2xx.

Windowing & aggregation rules:
- Primary contract window: 30-day rolling window aligned to UTC calendar days unless customer requests a different alignment in SOW.
- Short-term measurement window for burstability: 5-minute sliding windows to detect transient drops; transient drops that recover within a configured burst-bucket (see credits) do not count against long-term error budget unless repeated.
- Reporting granularity: 1-minute bucketing internally, 1-hour and 30-day aggregated reports for customer dashboards.

Error-budget model and crediting matrix (example):
- Define error budget E for window W as: E = max(0, CommittedTokensInW - ObservedTokensInW).
- Creditable percentage P based on severity of breach during W:
  - Minor shortfall (OCTR in [0.98,0.99)): 10% of E credited in dollars up to a cap of 1% of monthly invoice.
  - Moderate shortfall (OCTR in [0.95,0.98)): 30% of E credited or remediation plan initiation.
  - Major shortfall (OCTR < 0.95): 100% of E credited as service credit plus automatic escalation; additionally, customer may request a one-time termination right after cure period.
- Burst-bucket rule: customers can purchase an optional burst-bucket allowance (e.g., 20% of committed tokens per 24-hour period) which absorbs short transient oversubscription without affecting OCTR.
- Credit computation example (contract clause ready):
  "If the ObservedCommittedThroughputRatio for a Contract Month is below the threshold in Section X, Redwood Inference will issue a credit equal to the product of (a) the percentage specified in the Credit Table, (b) the dollar value of the shortfall tokens, and (c) the applicable monthly invoice. Credits will not exceed the cap specified in the Credit Table. Credits are the sole and exclusive monetary remedy for throughput degradation except as otherwise agreed in this Agreement."

Interaction with autoscaling and fleet controls:
- Autoscaling policy class: Guaranteed (no autoscale without prewarmed capacity), Elastic (automatically scales within reserved pool up to burst bucket), and Best-Effort (no SLA). Contracts must state which class applies.
- For Guaranteed pools: latency and throughput SLOs are primary; any reduction due to maintenance windows must be pre-notified and excluded from credit calculation if notice provided per contract.
- For Elastic pools: apply a short ramp window (default 2 minutes) where burst under-provisioning is tolerated and only long-term deficits count toward credits.
- Fleet control gestures (manual node drains, scheduled maintenance): these must be communicated and show up in the incident log. If a scheduled action reduces available capacity without customer notice, the related minutes are counted against OCTR.

Operational runbook summary (for Customer Success / Billing / Reliability):
- Automated detection: weekly and daily jobs compute OCTR and E; anomalies trigger a "throughput-breach" signal in PagerDuty on severity-major.
- Validation steps before issuing credit: (1) validate telemetry integrity (no ingestion gaps), (2) check for customer-side throttling or misconfiguration, (3) confirm autoscaling policies and recent deployment rollouts, (4) look for scheduled maintenance exclusions.
- Communication cadence: initial notification within 24 hours of first detection, provisional report within 3 business days, final determination and credits applied within 15 business days.

Suggested SOW language snippets (contract-friendly):
- Commitment paragraph: "Redwood Inference shall provide Dedicated Throughput to Customer equal to the committed tokens per month as set forth in Exhibit A. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain ObservedCommittedThroughputRatio at or above 99% measured over each 30-day Contract Month."
- Credit table example: include tiers mapping OCTR ranges to credit fractions and caps.
- Remedies: define systemic remediation, right to terminate for material failure, and SLA exclusion clauses (force majeure, customer misconfigurations, marketplace outages).

Open questions & decisions required:
- Do we default to 30-day rolling windows universally or allow customers to select shorter/longer windows at purchase? (Impact: billing complexity, susceptibility to transient events).
- Standard credit caps: should the default cap be 1% of monthly invoice or higher for enterprise deals?
- Legal signoff needed on "termination right" language for Major shortfall; coordinate with Legal on examples of cure periods and notice requirements.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- Draft contract language and credit table approved by Legal and Sales.
- Internal runbook steps and automation tickets created (ENG-9201 referenced) for daily/weekly OCTR computation.
- Customer-facing documentation (Console explainer + FAQ) drafted and reviewed by DX.
- A pilot customer agreement with the new language executed or at least verbally agreed to by Sales engineering.
